decisions.reason: As a newly launched drainage core component with its own product page, the polymer concrete drain housing fits the firm's engineering-led, durable system portfolio and is unlikely to be withdrawn so quickly.
A floor-level shower drainage system is central to the firm's stated direction toward modern, accessible bathroom drainage, so management would almost certainly continue backing it.
The designer shower drainage product matches the firm's design-conscious positioning and had dedicated website presentation, making an early discontinuation improbable.
The shower element with integrated slope directly supports easier installation and renovation use cases, which are strategic priorities for the firm, so it would likely be retained.

The backflow-protected basement floor drain addresses a clear technical problem and was explicitly presented as a developed solution, suggesting the firm would keep it on the market despite its more niche application.

The air-admittance valve is somewhat less central to the firm's visible shower-drainage focus and was only mentioned rather than strongly featured, but it still complements the broader drainage offering and would more likely be kept than dropped.
